name: Mashed Potatoes
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 60 ml/¼ cup milk, half-and-half, or light cream

steps: Peel the potatoes and dice them into pieces about 2–3 cm/1 inch thick.
Place the potatoes with about 1 tbsp of salt into a pot and add about 1.5 L/1½ quarts of water.
Boil the potatoes for about 15–20 minutes or until tender, then drain.
Either: Put through a potato ricer, then stir in the butter and milk or cream; or
Add the butter and milk or cream, then mash with a potato masher.
Add salt, pepper and (if you like) nutmeg to taste.

culture.text: Mashed potato or mashed potatoes, colloquially known as mash, is a dish made by mashing boiled or steamed potatoes, usually with added milk, butter, salt, and pepper. It is generally served as a side dish to meat or vegetables. Roughly mashed potatoes are sometimes called smashed potatoes. Dehydrated instant mashed potatoes and frozen mashed potatoes are available. Mashed potatoes are an ingredient in other dishes, such as dumplings and gnocchi.
